A game for the tyrant in all of us, I have spent many happy hours as the Holy Roman Empire (In reality it was not holy, not Roman and barely an empire but still my favourite faction) taxing the peasants into starvation to pay for my castles and my army. I have fought wars with just about everyone, been excommunicated four times and I have enjoyed every moment of it.

This is a game that I would recommend for some murderous medieval fun and mayhem, with a smattering of history thrown in (but not too much) and some great names, i.e. Frederich the Malevolent etc. which just add a nice little touch.

I've always liked this game. I can remember the initial purchase standing in some computer store.... CompUSA or something similar and I had to stand there for a LONG time reading every word on the physical cd rom case with artwork and all that...

It's a fantastic game even at its current age. I recommend it. Most of my play hours with this title was 10 pc's ago but I just realized as I am reinstalling it that I never reviewed it here on Steam. GREAT GAME.

We are all one
-Medieval II Total War End Credits
I know you fight for god.
And you believe it's right.
To rescue your home your life,
to face the evil night.
But in the darkest night when our children are asleep.
I think about the families,
of our enemy.
Do they feel the same,
believe their own truth?
They must love the children,
as faithfully as we do.
We all share one thing,
our hearts were given from above.
The only thing worth fighting for,
In this world is love.
On and on, through the years,
the war continues on.
Why can't we say the truth?
We are all one.
It's a good game, brings back good memories of wanting to play this game when i was a child. Good campaign, it can be very fun.

The game has gotten better since I got a new computer with savings. Before you play this you should play rome tw as it has many of the elements of this game and will teach you the basics if you are new. My previous review stated there was a "unspecified error" so you may want to make sure your computer isn't to old. Now this is a good game and worth it when it goes on steam sale, but before you play you may want to change desc_strat to 1 turn to 1060-1700 years (540 turns), otherwise the generals die too soon, as the years and unlock all faction as the game is a bit rushed in vinila. This will give enough turns to win the game comfortably. It has good buildings and is improved over rome and lets you take your country and use wish fullfilment to color the world one color. unlike rome buildings are ballanced more evenly but still some factions have more buildings than others in base game, which is kinda unfair since number of faction buildings should be ballanced imo. The problem with rome was that some factions lacked full buildings like barbarians. Some factions harder to play as. Start with england as channel protects you but also try others later to keep things new as nations which are surrounded are easier to get trade rights before you kill everyone.

Awesome RTS. Music, play, events, tactics, love it. Alos, amazing modding community. The only things I dont like are the mirco-managment of some units as well as how the AI will attack you for no reason sometimes... that can get repetitive having to fend of peasant enemy armies. but hey, this is Total War. 90% in my book.

Med 2 while a bit on the older side the base game will provide hours of fun, If I had to recommend mods I suggest Stainless Steel or the Third age and Divide and conquer, Stainless Steel being close enough to base game to remain the in the realm of history if that is important to you while Third Age and Divide and Conquer are Lord of the rings themed mods Divide and Conquer being my personal choice when it comes down to it.
Overall I can recommend this game so long as you don't mind its age.

I still play Third Age Total War to this day. This was the pinnacle of Grand Strategy when it came out and with the slew of mods out there, it holds up decently (not AAA, but a lot better than some.)

Arguably the most influential Grand Strategy game and best in the Total War series along with a very close Rome: Total War and its expansions.

Base game graphics are dated, but it is still playable and enjoyable to this day.

This game is the pinnacle of what makes shit great, a very interesting and dynamic combination of many medieval factions, send your armies storming across Europe like a Grand strategy game, but then when two collide switch to real time mode and command the battle from afar like Sabutai. Game manages to look decent yet still run very well on lower end comps. Definitely a must have.

Game is basically perfect mix of strategy, tactics and arcade tactics... until the late game when the artillery becomes ubiqutous. Because apparently, mangonels were the M117 howitzers equivalent, and unless you want all battles to be contests between two artillery doomstacks, the game turns into an exercise in frustration.

Excellent game, great gameplay, easy controls, but the battle commands are a bit different for those who play the game for the first time, it spoils the game a bit, also the failure to order online, spoils the game, but otherwise the game is 100%. 8.5 / 10

PROs:
Realistic Graphics (Way better than Empire Total War, and Empire Total War came after this)
Unlike Empire Total War, enemies have Hitpoints and don't fully rely on skill. Numbers also matter this time.
Nice Religious mechanics
Crusades
Jihads
Funny cutscenes (EX: Assassin drops a snake and it chases a rat and he chases after the snake.)
Able to play as Scotland
Be an English dog and make allies with France (and then get betrayed)
Thrilling siege battles
Its also a thrill to watch large ass mosh pits full of spearmen and swordsmen constantly hacking at each other
Many factions to play as
Many units to command

CONs:
No naval gameplay

10/10

Great historical turn-based simulator. Deals with military, economic, and religious issues during 1100 AD. Best of total war series.

You can forget about the other Total war games, you found the good one.

You will experience a 2006 game with all of it's 2006 clunk. However, behind the clunk and old graphics is a tremendous Total war Campaign. One that has sparked the desire for a Total war Medieval 3 for almost 2 decades now.

If you aren't sure, just test out the demo which will bring you through a historical battle to show you the ropes. I highly recommend you give this game a real go if you're a fan of the middle ages, strategy, knights, all of the above

Edit: If they mess Medieval 3 up, "They'll wish they've never been born sire!"

One of the best historical titles Creative Assembly has created, this game is still amazing to play after so many hours. Armies that don't need generals so you can send a small scout force or send reinforcements without needing a commander with them, the ability to trade cities and castles for money, crusades(DEUS VULT)/Jihads, and a couple of late game enemies that can provide a challenge when you get to the point where you can steamroll everyone else. Not only that, the mods for this game are insane like the Lord of the Rings mod Third Age: Total War and the submod Divide and Conquer or Stainless Steel 6.4 which adds more variety to the base game. Must get for those who don't care too much about the mid 2000s graphics for a great price!
I just wish that... you would release medieval III, and don't stop there... thank you for this, the ideology, creativity, production, quality, it is sheer entertainment at gaming peak level.
Hi. Probably the best thing about the game is its music. Makes the game feel like real dark ages. :-) At least for me!
This is the total war franchise at it's finest. There is diversity in unit types and civilizations, gameplay is well balanced and it runs very smoothly.

The campaign in this game is design for you to lose, no matter which way you go about it or what difficulty you place. For each army you slaughter that empire will breed another two or three out of nowhere, while you either have no time or funds to expand yours. Think you've defended your city from a siege? Guess again. While you were busy dealing with that one army, another empire will come and take the city as you are busy exterminating the first army. And just when you beaten all the counters and are about to put an empire out of commission and have the siege almost ready to begin, the game is like nope, we are gonna have your captain and army commit treason and leave you out in the open. Don't get me wrong, I love this game and love the battle tactics, but holy hell I've never been screwed so much in a game.

Half the time is map management and cursing the AI's politics.

The other half is realizing, that you forgot to send reinforcements to one particulary army in France.
My favorite game. I wish the they make a remake soon. Would be great to see this masterpiece running in a newer game engine.

I love this game and I recommend it to everyone who's wondering if it's worth it, yes it is. Here's a list of the pros and the cons of the game

Pros:
- decent graphics
- lots of missions
- lots of factions to choose from
- different battlegrouds, weather,forests,mountains, you can use pretty much everything in your advantage
- lots of town/castle upgrades
- lots of troops
- combat animations
- lots of campaigns (normal one, american, British Isles, etc)
- fun to play
- lots of mods for this game
- Multiplayer feature, you can fight against other players and find out new strategies
------------------------------------------------
Cons:
- Buggy
- May cause crashes
- laggy sometimes when there are more than 3500-4000 soldiers on the battlefield
- Boring after the turn of 100 when you capture all of Europe
- Allies will always backstab you, diplomacy is pretty much useless
- careful with the huge unit scale, it might cause lag on the battle map
- gunpowder Infantry is pretty much useless (for me at least), don't get them

Overall it's a good game, it works and it's fun to play even tho it'll cause crashed and lag sometimes. You should buy it, it has lots of campaigns, it'll keep you busy, It might help you out with your boringness if you're into this type of games

Probably the greatest Total War game to ever be released. Shame it didn't get the advertising campaign like Rome: Total War did. Truly an underappreciated masterpiece. My biggest wish is that Creative Assembly can achieve this level of mastery once again. If you can withstand graphics from 2006, I highly suggest playing it.

As you build your kingdom over the course of 400 years, don't forget to discover America, declare a Crusade/Jihad, assassinate the last 3 heirs of a family line to take over half of their kingdom, use your recently converted christian populace to stir up unrest and rebellion in the local muslim kingdom or vice versa, develop gunpowder, have one of your priests elected pope, get excommunicated, have your merchants systematically take advantage of another nation's trade resources, assassinate your own king, and watch as everything you worked for crumbles when the Black Death hits. This game had it all.

Very fun and easy to play RTS. Diplomacy, trade and war. If it is your first time playing, beware the Timurids they are very difficult to deal with until you figure out the best way to beat them. Same goes for the Mongols.

old school CA was so cool and they had lot of fun making this game back in the day. This game is pure art, honest work by a much of engineers and designers. Nothing can come ever close to the systems designed in this game. Every design decision just makes sense. there is no abstraction and hiding of info, every info can be easily accessed and the game hides nothing. pure gold and must buy on full price. The vanilla game without mods is plenty good and ton of fun and after 10000s of hrs with vanilla game you can have another 100000s of hours with mods.

while its fun to play if you are a fan of the total war series the gameplay does lack. for me a big downside is you get no time building a defence, most armies will reach your city in 1 turn making organizing a defence impossible also while under siege not being able to build troops is a weird decision because while under siege people get trained to fight. so many aspects could have been done better with just normal thinking. even mods don't really fix this, i don't know if its just not possible to change or they just don't so i won't give judgement on that. huge potential but limited execution.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players love the mods and customization, plus the gameplay and combat.
